First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C
$$

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\sqrt{3}/3}^{\infty }\frac{8}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{\sqrt{3}/3}^{a}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡x\,{|}_{\sqrt{3}/3}^{a} \\  & =8\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})) \\  & =8\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)-\frac{\pi }{6})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x,$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡x=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/28afd0a065525cd225377165c2164a1ecc254b1be8aba60d64324d14430c3be4.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\sqrt{3}/3}^{\infty }\frac{8}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =8\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =8\cdot \frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{8\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
